sentences.text: Rivian went from no revenue in FY2020 to $5,387 million in FY2025, a 48.1% three-year CAGR from FY2022 [F2][F7][D342].
The step change came in FY2022, when revenue rose 2914.5% to $1,658 million as deliveries began [F4][D83].
Growth then slowed to 12.1% in FY2024 and 8.4% in FY2025 as Automotive revenue fell 14.6% on 9,332 fewer deliveries, partly from the expiration of 45W tax credits [F6][F7][D187][D239][D315][P22].
The operating loss narrowed from $6,856 million in FY2022 to $3,585 million in FY2025, and gross margin turned positive at 2.7% [F23][F26][F19].
Software and services supplied the FY2025 growth, contributing 21.6pp on 221.7% growth to $1,557 million, or 28.9% of revenue [D295][D294][S14][D293].
That jump came from vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Volkswagen joint venture, plus remarketing and repair and maintenance [P18][P27].
New electric vehicles fell 12.5% and subtracted 10.5pp, leaving that product at 67.6% of revenue [D287][D288][D286].
Operating costs grew 6.9% against 8.4% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin was 264.7% [D258][D239][D265].
Diluted shares rose 17.1% while the net loss fell 23.2%, so EPS improved 34.5% to -$3.07 [D260][D241][D243][F57].
Operating margin of -66.5% is the window high but still far below the -129.4% median [F31][D325][D326].
In FY2025 the gross margin gain of 26.8pp drove the 27.8pp operating-margin improvement, while SG&A cost 0.5pp [D252][D253][D269].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0% on fewer vehicles produced and lower raw material and conversion costs [D255][P21].
SG&A rose 9.9% on go-to-market expansion, higher payroll and stock-based bonus accruals [D257][P13].
Net margin trailed operating margin by 1.1pp, as a $186 million securities litigation settlement lifted other expense [D359][P10].
Operating cash flow was -$779 million and free cash flow -$2,489 million, a -46.2% FCF margin against a -132.9% median [F64][F78][D226][D335].
The operating outflow shrank because of a significant reduction in net loss [P4].
Capex rose 49.9% to $1,710 million, 31.7% of revenue and 2.18x D&A, on Normal Factory capacity expansion [D246][F71][D225][D228][P3].
Stock-based compensation was $741 million, 20.7% of the operating loss, so cash burn understates the economic cost [X56][D237].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million from $16,907 million in FY2021 as cash and investments dropped 21.0% to $6,082 million [D231][D39][D261][D229].
The current ratio fell to 2.33x, the window low, as current liabilities grew 64.1% [F129][D339][D251].
FY2025 financing brought $886 million, mainly $750 million of stock issued to Volkswagen [F92][P2].
Equity fell 30.0% to $4,594 million and return on average equity was -65.4%, against a -7.9% peer median [D249][F142][D238][D354].
Rivian has posted a net loss in each of the last seven years, from -$426 million in FY2019 to -$3,646 million in FY2025 [R1][F32][F38].
Stock-based compensation has stayed at or above 10% of revenue for five years and was 13.8% in FY2025 [R2][D223].
Cash and investments cover 2.4 years of the latest burn, down from 4.1 years in FY2021 [R3][D236][D44].
The core new electric vehicle line fell 12.5% and is 67.6% of revenue, so the top line now leans on lower-margin services [R4][D287][D286].
Product revenue members sum to 129% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so segment shares should not be added [R6].
Whether gross margin holds above the FY2025 2.7% level or slips back toward the -24.1% of FY2024, reported in the FY2026 10-K [F19][F18].
Whether operating cash flow narrows past the FY2025 -$779 million toward breakeven, or widens again [F64].
Whether net cash stays above the FY2025 $1,642 million or the burn forces more financing [D231].
